title: An exhausted dispatch walk that met a quota wall is a capacity outcome, whatever the rung order
summary: From wave 24 (cycles 1733, 1734; design doc §5.11 T2). The runner surfaces the last rung's error (llmroute.DispatchTiered returns the last launch), and core.isQuotaWall defers only on exit 85. With the incapable ollama rung gone (T1), a walk [claude 81, codex 85] ends on the wall and defers, but [codex 85, claude 81] (codex's bench expired between walks) ends on claude's stall and FAILs, although no capable family could run the phase. The retrospectives of 1687 and 1734 name this.
acceptance: A walk that exhausted every candidate on fallback-trigger exits, at least one of them a quota wall, surfaces as a capacity outcome and the cycle defers (all_families_exhausted), for either rung order (tests)
A walk whose last capable rung failed for a non-trigger reason still surfaces that reason
The Signal Center line names every rung's exit
consumed_by: console landing fix/chain-plans-only-capable-drivers (2026-09-28): BUILT in the same landing that filed it. DispatchTiered.Walled + bridgechain.WallKeeper (runner and bridge handle alike) surface the wall of an exhausted walk whatever the rung order, naming every rung; a walk with no wall, or a non-trigger failure after a wall, still surfaces its own error; the quota pause carries the named walk into the quota.paused Signal Center line. Tests: TestDispatchTiered_AnExhaustedWalkThatMetAWallIsWalled, TestWallKeeper_SurfacesTheWallOfAWalledWalkNamingEveryRung, TestWalking_*, TestRun_AnExhaustedWalkThatMetAWallSurfacesTheWall, TestRun_AWallThenARealFailureSurfacesTheFailure.
